_comment: Starting point for the week 4 quiz. The questions below are drawn from what was actually taught in the week 4 sessions, but you should review and extend them before publishing — set isPublished to true when you are happy. Copy this file per module.
title: Understanding 5D BIM
intro: Five questions on quantification. You can retake this as many times as you like — the explanations are the point.

questions.prompt: You are given two drawings at different scales on the same PDF sheet. What should you do before taking off?
options: Scale to the larger drawing and measure both
Crop the sheet into separate pages and scale each one
Measure both and average the results
Scale to the smaller drawing and apply a correction factor
questions.explanation: Never measure two drawings at different scales on one page. Crop as New Page, then calibrate each separately — otherwise every quantity from one of them is wrong.

questions.prompt: After calibrating a drawing, what is a quick way to sanity-check that the scale is right?
options: Check that the sheet size matches the title block
Measure a wall and see whether its thickness matches the specified thickness
Compare the file size to the original
Re-run the calibration on a different line
questions.explanation: If a 225 mm wall measures 225 mm, the scale is right. It is the fastest check available and it costs nothing.

questions.prompt: Which tool is the right choice for taking off from a 3D model rather than a 2D drawing?
options: PlanSwift area tools
CostX dimension groups
Revit Schedules and Quantities
A manual dimension sheet
questions.explanation: Different software for different use cases. 2D drawings go to PlanSwift or CostX; a model already carries its quantities, and Schedules and Quantities reads them directly.

questions.prompt: In a Revit schedule, what does adding a calculated parameter such as width × height × count give you?
options: A new model element
A derived quantity such as total door area, without leaving the schedule
A change to the door family
A clash detection report
questions.explanation: Calculated parameters derive quantities from parameters the model already holds — no export, no spreadsheet, and it updates when the model does.

questions.prompt: Why does grouping a Revit wall schedule by base constraint matter to a quantity surveyor?
options: It makes the schedule shorter
It produces quantities floor by floor, which is how the bill is structured
It is required before exporting to Excel
It changes the wall type
questions.explanation: Base constraint is the level a wall sits on, so grouping by it splits the takeoff per floor — which is how a multi-storey bill has to be presented anyway.
